summary.title: siem-docker-stack threat model
summary.description: Threat model of the docker-compose SIEM stack (OpenSearch hot/warm, Logstash, syslog-ng, Grafana, InfluxDB, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Wazuh, optional CrowdSec/UniFi Poller/Portainer) built from docker/docker-compose.yml, docker/*/ configs, scripts/ and n8n/ workflows at origin/master. No LLM or AI component exists in the stack (n8n/ideas.md mentions local LLMs only as ideas). Updated for issue #32: threats 14, 27, 28, 29 and 32 are Mitigated; other descriptions that say a port is published on all interfaces describe the stack before that change.

data.name: Untrusted network (LAN, log senders, agents, operators)
data.description: Everything that can reach the published host ports. Docker-published ports bypass UFW (comment in docker/docker-compose.yml opensearch-hot; scripts/02-bootstrap.sh firewall section), so the host firewall is not a reliable boundary.

data.name: SIEM host: Docker siem-net (single flat bridge)
data.description: One bridge network for all services (networks.siem-net in docker/docker-compose.yml). No per-service network segmentation.

data.name: Host OS and Docker daemon (bind mounts, secrets, key material)
data.description: Bind-mounted /data/hot, /data/warm, .env, certs and the Docker socket. Evidence: volumes sections in docker/docker-compose.yml.

data.name: External services (not defined in compose)
data.description: n8n, Discord, VirusTotal, UniFi controller. n8n is referenced as http://n8n/webhook/... (wazuh/integrations/custom-n8n, docker/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml) but is not a service in docker/docker-compose.yml.

data.name: Supply chain and CI
data.description: Container registries and GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/*.yml).

data.name: Network devices (pfSense, Suricata, UniFi)
data.description: Send syslog (UDP/TCP 514) and Suricata EVE JSON (UDP 5140). Evidence: docker/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf sources; docker/logstash/pipeline/01-suricata.conf header.

data.name: Arbitrary LAN host or attacker
data.description: Any host that can reach the published ports. Syslog and EVE ingestion have no sender authentication (syslog-ng.conf s_network_udp/s_network_tcp; 01-suricata.conf udp input).

data.name: Wazuh agents
data.description: Connect to 1514 (events) and 1515 (enrollment) published by wazuh-manager in docker/docker-compose.yml.

data.name: Operator / analyst browser
data.description: Uses Grafana :3000, OpenSearch Dashboards :5601, Wazuh Dashboard :443, Prometheus :9090, Portainer :9443 (ports in docker/docker-compose.yml).

data.name: Maintainer (deploy over SSH)
data.description: Runs scripts/03-deploy.sh over SSH, change-passwords.sh and 08b-init-opensearch-security.sh on the host; pushes PRs.

data.name: syslog-ng
data.description: balabit/syslog-ng:${SYSLOG_NG_VERSION:-latest}; receives 514 UDP/TCP raw (flags(no-parse)), archives, forwards to Logstash and Wazuh. No user: directive, owner(root) in syslog-ng.conf options. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml syslog-ng; docker/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf.

threats.title: syslog-ng runs as root with default container privileges
threats.description: Evidence: syslog-ng.conf options owner(root); docker/docker-compose.yml syslog-ng has no user:, cap_drop or read_only. It parses untrusted network input. Impact bounded by the container, but no hardening directives exist anywhere in docker/docker-compose.yml (searched for cap_drop, security_opt, read_only, privileged, mem_limit, pids_limit: none).

data.name: Logstash
data.description: opensearch logstash-oss 8.9.0; inputs udp 5140 (json) and tcp 5045 (json_lines); filter dissect/grok/kv/json; opensearch output as user logstash with CA-verified TLS. Evidence: docker/logstash/pipeline/*.conf; logstash.yml (http.host 0.0.0.0, persisted queue 1gb, DLQ).

threats.title: Message-embedded headers override program/host and steer routing and parsing
threats.description: Evidence: 02-syslog.conf. When message starts with <PRI>1, dissect/grok output replaces program, source_host and message (mutate replace), and routing keys on program == filterlog, program =~ crowdsec and source_host =~ pfsense|unifi. Sender-controlled text therefore selects the index and the CrowdSec json/kv parsing path, and kv/json-parsed fields (crowdsec.source_ip, crowdsec.value) are promoted to source.ip. Fabricated entries can pollute alert counts and enrichment queries (the n8n crowdsec workflow aggregates message.keyword). No validation or allowlist of those fields in the pipeline.

threats.title: Flooding UDP/TCP ingest and regex cost on attacker-controlled text
threats.description: Evidence: no rate limiting in syslog-ng.conf or the pipelines; persisted queue capped at 1gb and DLQ enabled (logstash.yml), so a flood fills the queue and applies backpressure or drops UDP. grok/dissect/kv run on attacker text (02-syslog.conf); UNVERIFIED whether any pattern backtracks badly. Detective control only: Prometheus alerts IngestRateZero and FilesystemFillingUp (docker/prometheus/rules/siem-health.yml).

threats.title: Logstash to OpenSearch uses TLS with CA verification and a scoped role
threats.description: Evidence: outputs in 01-suricata.conf and 02-syslog.conf; docker/opensearch/security/roles.yml logstash_writer.
threats.mitigation: 01-suricata.conf and 02-syslog.conf outputs set ssl_certificate_verification true with cacert; roles.yml logstash_writer is limited to write/create_index on the SIEM index patterns plus template put; roles_mapping.yml maps only user logstash.

data.name: OpenSearch hot node
data.description: opensearchproject/opensearch 2.19.0; security plugin on, HTTP and transport TLS, anonymous auth off. Evidence: docker/opensearch/opensearch-hot.yml; docker/opensearch/security/config.yml.

threats.title: Anonymous or unauthenticated access to the main OpenSearch cluster
threats.description: Evidence: docker/opensearch/security/config.yml, opensearch-hot.yml, healthcheck in docker/docker-compose.yml expects 401.
threats.mitigation: security/config.yml sets anonymous_auth_enabled false; HTTP and transport TLS enabled in opensearch-hot.yml/opensearch-warm.yml; nodes_dn and admin_dn pinned; users hashed with bcrypt via scripts/08b-init-opensearch-security.sh and internal_users.yml is gitignored; scripts/08b verifies an unauthenticated request returns 401.

threats.title: Credential guessing against exposed OpenSearch login with no lockout or MFA configured
threats.description: Evidence: 9200 published on all interfaces (docker/docker-compose.yml); security/config.yml defines only basic and clientcert authc, no auth_failure_listeners/blocking and no SSO/MFA; same applies to 9201 (warm) and 9202 (Wazuh indexer). UPDATE (issue #32): OpenSearch 9200 and Dashboards 5601 now bind to BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 default); no lockout or MFA was added.

threats.title: Admin client key is mounted into the running hot node and CA/admin certs are long-lived
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml opensearch-hot mounts admin.pem and admin-key.pem; opensearch-hot.yml authcz.admin_dn trusts CN=admin; scripts/07-generate-opensearch-certs.sh issues 3650-day RSA-2048 certs and chmod 640 on keys. Anyone who reads those key files from the container or host gets all_access via client-cert auth (clientcert_auth_domain in config.yml). The Wazuh indexer mounts its admin key similarly.

threats.title: Node transport hostname verification disabled
threats.description: Evidence: enforce_hostname_verification: false in opensearch-hot.yml and opensearch-warm.yml. Mitigating context: nodes_dn pins the allowed node DNs and certs come from one private CA.

data.name: OpenSearch warm node
data.description: Data/ingest node; port 9201 published on all interfaces; transport TLS to hot node. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml opensearch-warm; opensearch-warm.yml.

threats.title: Warm node HTTP port published on all interfaces
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml opensearch-warm ports 9201:9200 with no 127.0.0.1 prefix, unlike the transport ports. Protected only by the security plugin (basic auth).
threats.mitigation: docker/docker-compose.yml: opensearch-warm publishes ${BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:9201:9200, loopback by default; widening is an explicit BIND_ADDR change (README, Network exposure). Guarded by tests/python/test_compose_security.py.

data.name: Grafana
data.description: grafana-oss:${GRAFANA_VERSION:-latest}, user 472, installs plugins at start (GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS). Admin password from GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS with fallback. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml grafana.

threats.title: Grafana held InfluxDB and Wazuh indexer admin credentials
threats.description: Evidence (original finding): the grafana service received WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD and INFLUXDB_ADMIN_*, and datasources.yml used the Wazuh indexer admin and the InfluxDB admin, so a Grafana compromise (published :3000, latest image, plugins installed at start) could write or delete Wazuh and Influx data, i.e. erase evidence. FIXED (issue #32), both halves. InfluxDB: Grafana uses a read-only account (GRAFANA_INFLUX_USER, GRANT READ on pfsense/unpoller/telegraf) created by the influxdb bootstrap in docker/docker-compose.yml. Wazuh indexer: the OpenSearch-Wazuh datasource uses WAZUH_GRAFANA_RO_USER (default grafana_ro) with role wazuh_grafana_readonly, read-only on wazuh-alerts-*, wazuh-archives-*, wazuh-monitoring-* and wazuh-statistics-*; the grafana service no longer receives WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD. Checked every datasource in datasources.yml: the four main-cluster OpenSearch ones use the readonly user, InfluxDB and InfluxDB-UniFi use the read-only Influx user, Prometheus has no credential; none uses an admin account. Residual: the Wazuh account is provisioned at deploy time by running scripts/11-wazuh-grafana-readonly.sh; until it runs, the Wazuh datasource cannot log in (fails closed). Port 3000 binds to BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 default). Grafana still holds read access to the data, and the indexer certificate is not verified (tlsSkipVerify).
threats.mitigation: docker/wazuh/security/{roles,roles_mapping,internal_users}.fragment.yml define the read-only role, mapping and user; scripts/11-wazuh-grafana-readonly.sh bcrypt-hashes WAZUH_GRAFANA_RO_PASSWORD inside wazuh-indexer, merges the fragments into the in-container security config, applies them with securityadmin.sh and checks read 200 / delete 403; docker/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml uses $WAZUH_GRAFANA_RO_USER/$WAZUH_GRAFANA_RO_PASSWORD; docker/docker-compose.yml grafana env has WAZUH_GRAFANA_RO_PASSWORD (${VAR:?}) and no WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD. tests/python/test_compose_security.py asserts no datasource uses an admin account and that the role allows read actions only.

threats.title: Unpinned Grafana image and plugins installed at container start
threats.description: Evidence: grafana/grafana-oss:${GRAFANA_VERSION:-latest}; GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS=grafana-opensearch-datasource,grafana-clock-panel,grafana-worldmap-panel with no versions, fetched on each start from the plugin catalog.

threats.title: Log content rendered in dashboards (stored XSS or panel injection)
threats.description: UNVERIFIED: log fields such as message and source_host are stored unmodified (02-syslog.conf does no sanitizing) and rendered by Grafana and OpenSearch Dashboards panels. Whether current versions escape every panel type was not tested here.

threats.title: Known fallback passwords across the stack (Grafana, OpenSearch users, Influx, UniFi)
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml uses ${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS:-changeme}, ${OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD:-changeme-dashboards}, ${OPENSEARCH_LOGSTASH_PASSWORD:-changeme-logstash}, ${OPENSEARCH_READONLY_PASSWORD:-changeme-readonly}, ${INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-changeme-influx}, ${UNIFI_PASS:-changeme}; logstash pipelines default to changeme-logstash; deploy scripts default GRAFANA_PASS to changeme. 08b-init-opensearch-security.sh refuses to run with missing OpenSearch passwords (it checks each variable), but the compose file itself does not, so containers can start with the public defaults for the other services.
threats.mitigation: docker/docker-compose.yml: every secret (GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS, OPENSEARCH_*_PASSWORD, INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD, UNIFI_PASS, WAZUH_*_PASSWORD) uses ${VAR:?}, so `docker compose config` fails with a message naming the variable; docker/logstash/pipeline/*.conf read ${OPENSEARCH_LOGSTASH_PASSWORD} with no default (Logstash fails to start if unset); scripts/05-verify.sh requires WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD. scripts/check-env.sh rejects placeholders; tests/python/test_compose_security.py fails on any secret-named `:-` fallback. Residual: client-side deploy scripts (scripts/deploy-*.py, deploy-n8n-soar.sh, 08-crowdsec-smoketest.sh) still default GRAFANA_PASS to changeme, which only matters if the server uses that password; .env.example still contains the old placeholder values (check-env.sh rejects them).

data.name: OpenSearch Dashboards
data.description: opensearch-dashboards 2.19.0 on :5601; no TLS config for the server side in repo; connects to hot node as kibanaserver with OPENSEARCH_SSL_VERIFICATIONMODE=none. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml opensearch-dashboards.

threats.title: Operator logins to Dashboards and Grafana travel over cleartext HTTP
threats.description: Evidence: no server.ssl for the main Dashboards container; GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=http://...; no Grafana TLS settings; ports published on all interfaces (docker/docker-compose.yml). Basic-auth admin credentials cross the LAN unencrypted unless a reverse proxy the repo does not provide is added.

data.name: InfluxDB 1.8
data.description: influxdb:1.8 on :8086, HTTP auth enabled, admin user bootstrapped by the container command. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml influxdb.

threats.title: InfluxDB published with a shared admin account
threats.description: Evidence: 8086 published on all interfaces and opened in ufw (02-bootstrap.sh); auth enabled (INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED=true); the same admin identity is reused by Grafana and unifi-poller, no per-service users. Plain HTTP (f_gf_inf, f_unifi_inf). UPDATE (issue #32): port 8086 now binds to INGEST_BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 default) and Grafana and unifi-poller use read-only and write-only accounts; the admin account still exists and any pfSense Telegraf writer set up outside the repo may still use it.

data.name: UniFi Poller (optional)
data.description: ghcr.io/unpoller/unpoller:${UNPOLLER_VERSION:-latest}; writes to InfluxDB as the InfluxDB admin; UP_UNIFI_DEFAULT_VERIFY_SSL=false. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml unifi-poller.

threats.title: UniFi controller TLS verification disabled; shared InfluxDB admin credentials
threats.description: Evidence: UP_UNIFI_DEFAULT_VERIFY_SSL=false, UNIFI_PASS fallback changeme, UP_INFLUXDB_USER/PASS use the InfluxDB admin (docker/docker-compose.yml unifi-poller). Image tag defaults to latest. UPDATE (issue #32): the UNIFI_PASS fallback is gone (required variable) and the poller now writes InfluxDB as UNPOLLER_INFLUX_USER (GRANT WRITE on unpoller only) instead of the admin. STILL OPEN: UP_UNIFI_DEFAULT_VERIFY_SSL=false and the latest image tag.

data.name: Prometheus
data.description: prom/prometheus:${PROMETHEUS_VERSION:-latest} on :9090 with --web.enable-lifecycle; no auth or TLS configured. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml prometheus; docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml.

threats.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus with lifecycle API on a published port
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml prometheus publishes 9090 on all interfaces with --web.enable-lifecycle and no web config file; scripts/02-bootstrap.sh ufw allows 9090. Any reachable host can read inventory (targets, labels, alert state) and POST /-/quit or /-/reload to stop or disrupt monitoring. UPDATE (issue #32): Prometheus 9090 now binds to BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 default); it is still unauthenticated with the lifecycle API enabled.

data.name: Alertmanager
data.description: prom/alertmanager v0.27.0, bound to 127.0.0.1:9093; routes critical and warning alerts to an n8n webhook. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml alertmanager; docker/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml.template.

threats.title: Alertmanager API exposure
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml alertmanager ports.
threats.mitigation: Port bound to 127.0.0.1 only (docker/docker-compose.yml alertmanager ports: 127.0.0.1:${ALERTMANAGER_PORT:-9093}:9093 with the comment 'no reason to expose').

data.name: elasticsearch-exporter
data.description: quay.io/prometheuscommunity/elasticsearch-exporter v1.7.0; holds the readonly password in env; --es.ssl-skip-verify. No host port. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml elasticsearch-exporter.

data.name: cAdvisor
data.description: gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor v0.49.1; mounts /, /var/run, /sys, /var/lib/docker read-only; no host port, not privileged in compose. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml cadvisor.

threats.title: cAdvisor reads host root filesystem and Docker state
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml cadvisor mounts /, /var/run, /sys and /var/lib/docker read-only; no host port, so reachable only from siem-net (Prometheus scrapes cadvisor:8080 per prometheus.yml). A compromised container on the network could read host paths through it. Not privileged in compose.

data.name: Wazuh manager
data.description: wazuh/wazuh-manager 4.9.2; publishes 1514 tcp/udp, 1515, 55000; env INDEXER_PASSWORD fallback SecretPassword; custom integrations dir bind-mounted writable. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml wazuh-manager.

threats.title: Default Wazuh credentials used when .env is incomplete
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml wazuh-manager/dashboard fall back to INDEXER_PASSWORD SecretPassword and API_PASSWORD MyS3cr3tP4ssw0rd via ${VAR:-default}; the compose file warns to change them. 1515, 55000 and the indexer port 9202 are published on all interfaces. A stack started without .env runs with publicly known credentials and compose does not fail.
threats.mitigation: docker/docker-compose.yml: WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD and WAZUH_API_PASSWORD are required variables (${VAR:?}), so compose refuses to start when .env is missing or incomplete; no SecretPassword/MyS3cr3tP4ssw0rd fallback remains. 1515/1514 bind to INGEST_BIND_ADDR and 55000/9202 to BIND_ADDR, both defaulting to 127.0.0.1. scripts/check-env.sh (run by scripts/03-deploy.sh) rejects empty values and the old defaults; tests/python/test_compose_security.py guards both. Residual: a value copied from the old .env.example that is not one of the listed defaults passes; `wazuh:wazuh` default API admin is still tried by change-passwords.sh.

data.name: Wazuh indexer
data.description: wazuh/wazuh-indexer 4.9.2; single node, TLS on; published on ${WAZUH_INDEXER_PORT:-9202} on all interfaces. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml wazuh-indexer; docker/wazuh/wazuh-indexer.yml.

data.name: Wazuh dashboard
data.description: wazuh/wazuh-dashboard 4.9.2 on :443 with TLS; connects to the indexer as kibanaserver with literal password kibanaserver in compose and opensearch_dashboards.yml. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml wazuh-dashboard; docker/wazuh/opensearch_dashboards.yml.

threats.title: Hard-coded kibanaserver/kibanaserver for the Wazuh dashboard
threats.description: Evidence: DASHBOARD_USERNAME=kibanaserver and DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=kibanaserver in docker/docker-compose.yml wazuh-dashboard, and opensearch.password: kibanaserver in docker/wazuh/opensearch_dashboards.yml. This is not read from .env; it changes only if change-passwords.sh is run (it seds DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in the compose file). Until then the default credential for the indexer service account is known and the indexer port 9202 is published on all interfaces. UNVERIFIED: whether the stock Wazuh indexer user database still holds the same default hash (not in the repo).
threats.mitigation: docker/docker-compose.yml: DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=${WAZUH_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD:?...} (required) and docker/wazuh/opensearch_dashboards.yml: opensearch.password: "${DASHBOARD_PASSWORD}" read from the environment; change-passwords.sh sets the matching kibanaserver hash on the Wazuh indexer and writes .env (not the compose file). Indexer port 9202 binds to BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 by default). Residual: on an existing deployment the indexer keeps the old hash until change-passwords.sh is run (README, Upgrade notes); UNVERIFIED against a live Wazuh indexer (no containers were run).

data.name: CrowdSec (optional, profile crowdsec)
data.description: crowdsecurity/crowdsec:${CROWDSEC_VERSION:-latest}; mounts host /var/log read-only; no user: directive. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml crowdsec; docker/crowdsec/acquis.yaml.

data.name: Portainer CE
data.description: portainer/portainer-ce:lts, mounts /var/run/docker.sock read-write, publishes 9443 on all interfaces. Labeled Optional in a comment but has no profile, so it starts with the default stack. Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml portainer.

threats.title: Portainer with read-write Docker socket starts by default on a public port
threats.description: Evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml portainer mounts /var/run/docker.sock read-write, publishes 9443 on all interfaces, has no profile (the crowdsec service has one; portainer does not) although commented Optional; scripts/02-bootstrap.sh leaves the 9443 ufw rule commented but Docker publishing bypasses ufw. Control of this UI is root on the host. Portainer's own first-run admin setup is the only gate (UNVERIFIED which timeout/lockdown applies in the lts image).
threats.mitigation: docker/docker-compose.yml: portainer has profiles: ["portainer"] so it does not start by default (`docker compose --profile portainer up -d portainer` to opt in) and publishes 9443 on ${PORTAINER_BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}. README "Portainer (opt-in)" documents enabling it. Residual: when enabled, the Docker socket is still mounted read-write, so anyone who can reach the UI (loopback by default) is root on the host.

data.name: Docker daemon
data.description: Host daemon behind /var/run/docker.sock; full control of the host for whoever can talk to it. Evidence: portainer and cadvisor volume mounts in docker/docker-compose.yml.

threats.title: Flat siem-net lets a compromised container reach every other service
threats.description: Evidence: single bridge network, no network segmentation; internal APIs (OpenSearch, InfluxDB, Prometheus, Logstash API with http.host 0.0.0.0 per logstash.yml, cAdvisor) are reachable from every container. Logstash 9600 has no ports entry in docker/docker-compose.yml so it is not published to the host, but is reachable in-network.

threats.title: No container hardening directives
threats.description: Evidence: searching docker/docker-compose.yml for cap_drop, security_opt, read_only, privileged, mem_limit and pids_limit found none. Containers keep Docker's default capability set; syslog-ng, crowdsec and others run with the image's default user. Only grafana (472), prometheus and alertmanager (65534) set user.

data.name: Syslog archive (/data/warm/archives/syslog)
data.description: Raw archived syslog files written by syslog-ng, perm 0640 owner root. Evidence: syslog-ng.conf options and destinations; docker/docker-compose.yml syslog-ng volumes. The config comment says rotated daily but no rotation config is in the repo.

threats.title: Unbounded archive growth fills the data disk
threats.description: Evidence: syslog-ng.conf writes per-day files with no size limit; the comment claims daily rotation but no rotation config exists in the repo. The only control is the Prometheus FilesystemFillingUp/FilesystemCritical alerts (siem-health.yml), which are detective.

threats.title: Audit and archive integrity depends on the same host and cluster
threats.description: Evidence: opensearch-hot.yml plugins.security.audit.type: internal_opensearch stores the audit log inside the cluster an admin can modify; archives are plain files with no signing or off-host copy in the repo; snapshots go to /data/warm/snapshots on the same host (opensearch-hot.yml path.repo, docker/docker-compose.yml volumes). An attacker with admin or root can alter evidence.

data.name: Secrets: .env and compose file
data.description: Passwords come from .env (gitignored per .gitignore) via ${VAR:-fallback} interpolation in docker/docker-compose.yml; change-passwords.sh also rewrites the compose file in place. Prometheus file_sd target files with LAN addresses are gitignored.

threats.title: Passwords live in container environment, compose file edits and command lines
threats.description: Evidence: secrets are env vars in docker/docker-compose.yml (visible via docker inspect to anyone with Docker access); change-passwords.sh passes the new password inside docker exec command strings (hash.sh -p '...', grafana cli admin reset-admin-password) so it appears in the host process list, and writes plaintext passwords into docker-compose.yml with sed (INDEXER_PASSWORD, DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, API_PASSWORD) and into .env (GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASS). Passwords containing quotes or | can also break the quoting. 08b-init-opensearch-security.sh is better: it passes HASH_PASS through docker exec -e. UPDATE (issue #32): change-passwords.sh no longer seds plaintext passwords into docker-compose.yml (all secrets are written to .env) and sends bcrypt-hash inputs, curl credentials and the wazuh.yml update to containers on stdin. STILL OPEN: secrets remain container environment variables (docker inspect), and the Grafana CLI reset still passes the new password on the docker exec command line.

threats.title: Secrets and LAN addresses committed to git
threats.description: Evidence: .gitignore, .github/workflows/security.yml.
threats.mitigation: .gitignore excludes .env, generated certs/keys, docker/opensearch/security/internal_users.yml (bcrypt hashes) and docker/prometheus/targets/*.json (real IPs); the template is tracked instead; security.yml (GYST) runs gitleaks per its header comment. Residual: the .gitleaksignore content was not reviewed.

data.name: TLS key material (docker/opensearch/certs, docker/wazuh/certs)
data.description: Root CA, node and admin keys generated by scripts/07-generate-opensearch-certs.sh and the Wazuh cert generator; gitignored (*.pem, *.key). 3650-day RSA-2048 certs.

data.name: Index and snapshot data (/data/hot, /data/warm)
data.description: OpenSearch indices, Wazuh data, InfluxDB, Prometheus TSDB, Grafana state, snapshots at /data/warm/snapshots. Evidence: volumes in docker/docker-compose.yml.

data.name: n8n (external)
data.description: Receives webhooks wazuh-alerts, grafana-alerts, crowdsec-alerts, alertmanager-siem (n8n/*.json, custom-n8n). Webhook nodes carry no authentication parameter. n8n's own deployment is not in this repo: UNVERIFIED how it is exposed.

threats.title: CrowdSec enrichment workflow queries OpenSearch without TLS or credentials
threats.description: Evidence: n8n/crowdsec-alert-enrichment.json node 'Query OpenSearch Bans' posts to http://opensearch-hot:9200/... with no credential, but the cluster now requires HTTPS and auth (config.yml). The enrichment path fails or is silently degraded, and fixing it by weakening cluster security would be a regression.

data.name: Discord (webhook)
data.description: Alert destination; credential referenced as n8n credential discordWebhookApi (n8n/*.json shows placeholder id YOUR_CREDENTIAL_ID).

threats.title: Discord webhook secret kept out of the repo
threats.description: Evidence: n8n/*.json discord nodes reference credential discordWebhookApi with placeholder id YOUR_CREDENTIAL_ID.
threats.mitigation: Workflow templates in n8n/*.json contain a credential reference placeholder, not the webhook URL; the URL lives in n8n's credential store.

data.name: VirusTotal API
data.description: wazuh/integrations/virustotal.py calls https://www.virustotal.com/vtapi/v2/file/report with the file hash.

threats.title: File hashes sent to VirusTotal; local cache is a trust input
threats.description: Evidence: wazuh/integrations/virustotal.py posts the hash to virustotal.com and caches results in SQLite under the manager's integrations directory (writable bind mount /data/hot/wazuh/manager/integrations). Hash disclosure to a third party is by design; anyone able to write the cache DB can pin a clean verdict for up to 7 days (TTL_MAP).

data.name: GitHub Actions CI (GYST callers)
data.description: ci.yml, security.yml, dependabot-auto-merge.yml call ChiefGyk3D/git-your-ship-together reusable workflows pinned by commit SHA with version comment; permissions contents: read; egress-policy block.

threats.title: Compromised workflow dependency or over-privileged CI token
threats.description: Evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml, security.yml, dependabot-auto-merge.yml.
threats.mitigation: Reusable workflows are pinned to a commit SHA with a version comment; top-level permissions contents: read with per-job grants; egress-policy block with an explicit endpoint list (ci.yml, security.yml); security.yml adds CodeQL (actions), dependency review and Scorecard. Residual: dependabot-auto-merge enables auto-merge on Dependabot PRs once the gate is green.

threats.title: Shell lint findings do not block CI
threats.description: Evidence: ci.yml sets the shellcheck and shfmt jobs to non-blocking (inputs shellcheck-continue-on-error and shfmt-continue-on-error, set to true) with a comment citing pre-existing findings. Script defects (for example quoting in change-passwords.sh) can merge unflagged.

data.name: Forged/flooded syslog
data.description: Same ports as f_dev_sys; the only source filter (f_network netmask 192.168.0.0/16) is applied to the Wazuh log path only, not to the Logstash/archive path (syslog-ng.conf log paths).

threats.title: Unauthenticated syslog lets any LAN host forge events
threats.description: Evidence: syslog-ng.conf s_network_udp/s_network_tcp accept anyone; the netmask filter is attached only to the Wazuh path; docker/docker-compose.yml publishes 514/udp and 514/tcp on all interfaces. A sender can impersonate pfSense or UniFi (host and program fields are sender-controlled) and inject fake firewall, auth or CrowdSec events that appear in dashboards and alerts. Syslog has no sender authentication; the repo has no allowlist at the published ports.

data.name: Forged/flooded EVE JSON UDP 5140
data.description: No sender authentication on the udp input (01-suricata.conf).

threats.title: Unauthenticated EVE JSON on UDP 5140 allows field injection
threats.description: Evidence: 01-suricata.conf udp input with json codec, no auth, published on all interfaces. Attacker-supplied JSON keys become event fields (timestamp, event_type, nested objects). UNVERIFIED: the input type setting does not overwrite an existing type field per Logstash documentation, so a sender may choose type and cause events to be dropped by the type == suricata output conditional; not run here.

data.name: JSON over TCP 5045

threats.title: Syslog forwarding to Logstash and Wazuh is plaintext on siem-net
threats.description: Evidence: syslog-ng.conf d_logstash tcp and d_wazuh udp have no TLS. Only reachable from containers on siem-net, so exposure needs a compromised container (see flat network threat).

threats.title: n8n webhooks accept unauthenticated alert posts over plain HTTP
threats.description: Evidence: n8n/*.json webhook nodes define only httpMethod and path, no authentication; callers (alertmanager.yml.template, wazuh/integrations/custom-n8n, deploy-n8n-soar.sh) use http:// with no auth header. Anyone who can reach the n8n webhook can forge alerts (alert fatigue, hiding real alerts via the dedup windows in wazuh-alert-triage.json) or replay payloads. UNVERIFIED: n8n network exposure and any reverse-proxy auth are outside this repo.

threats.title: Deploy over SSH and secrets on the command line
threats.description: Evidence: scripts/03-deploy.sh runs remote commands via ssh with BatchMode; deploy-n8n-soar.sh pipes secrets as a curl config on stdin so they stay off the remote command line (mitigating); GRAFANA_PASS defaults to changeme in deploy-n8n-soar.sh and deploy-grafana-alerts.py. Host key checking policy is the user's ssh config (not set in the scripts).

threats.title: Unpinned images and no image scanning or digest pinning
threats.description: Evidence: :latest or floating tags for grafana, prometheus, syslog-ng, unifi-poller, crowdsec (via ${..:-latest}), crowdsec/metabase and portainer lts in docker/docker-compose.yml and docker/crowdsec/docker-compose.crowdsec.yml; wazuh certs generated with wazuh/wazuh-certs-generator:latest. Pinned by tag (not digest): opensearch 2.19.0, logstash 8.9.0, wazuh 4.9.2, influxdb 1.8, alertmanager v0.27.0, exporter v1.7.0, cadvisor v0.49.1. .github/dependabot.yml covers github-actions only, so image tags are not auto-bumped; no image scan job is in the workflows.
